title: Are Gold Plated Earrings Worth It? Quality & Care Explained
metaTitle: Are Gold Plated Earrings Worth It? | Pearl Bloom
metaDescription: Are gold plated earrings worth it? We explain quality, durability, anti-tarnish coatings and care so you can buy gold-tone with confidence. Find out.
excerpt: Gold plated earrings give a real-gold look for a fraction of the price — but are they worth it? Here's the honest take on quality, durability and care.
bodyHtml:
Gold plated earrings promise the warm glow of gold for a fraction of the price. But are they actually worth buying, or will they fade in a month? Here is an honest look at what you get — and how to make them last.

What 'gold plated' really means

Gold plated means a fine layer of gold-tone plating is bonded over a durable base metal, then sealed. It is not solid gold and carries no hallmark — it is fashion jewellery designed to look luxe. The closely related gold-tone finish gives the same warm colour; the practical difference for most shoppers is small.

The case for gold plated earrings

The value is obvious: you get the look of gold across studs, hoops and festive designs for a tiny fraction of fine-jewellery prices. That means you can own many pairs, match earrings to specific outfits, and restyle freely as trends change. With an anti-tarnish seal, a good plated pair also holds its shine impressively well for daily wear.

The honest limitations

Plating is a surface, so it can wear over time, especially with heavy friction, moisture and chemical exposure. It has no resale or investment value, and it is not meant to be an heirloom. For most people, that trade-off is entirely worth it — you are buying everyday style, not bullion.

How to make them last

Care is what separates a pair that fades fast from one that lasts. Keep them dry, put them on after perfume, hairspray and skincare, avoid swimming and long hot showers in them, and wipe them gently after wear. Our care guide has the full routine. Do this, and gold plated earrings easily earn their place.

The verdict

For affordable, everyday-to-occasion style, gold plated earrings are absolutely worth it. Treat them as the wearable, refreshable fashion pieces they are — not as solid gold — and you get a premium look, real versatility and excellent value.

faqs.q: Are gold plated earrings worth buying?
faqs.a: For everyday and occasion style, yes. They give a real-gold look at a fraction of the price, hold their shine well with anti-tarnish coatings, and let you own many pairs affordably.

faqs.q: Do gold plated earrings fade or turn your ears green?
faqs.a: Quality anti-tarnish plated earrings resist fading and use skin-safe metal, so they should not turn ears green. Keeping them dry and off perfume and lotion makes the finish last much longer.

faqs.q: Are gold plated earrings real gold?
faqs.a: No. They have a thin layer of gold-tone plating over a base metal. They look like gold but are fashion jewellery — not solid gold and not hallmarked.

faqs.q: What is the difference between gold plated and gold tone?
faqs.a: Gold plated has an actual bonded layer of gold-tone metal over a core, while gold tone refers to any finish giving a gold colour. Both offer the gold look affordably.

title: Stud Earrings Guide: Everyday Styles That Go With Everything
metaTitle: Stud Earrings: Everyday Style Guide | Pearl Bloom
metaDescription: A simple guide to stud earrings — the everyday styles that go with everything, plus tips on comfort, care and building a daily stud rotation. Read on.
excerpt: The humble stud is the hardest-working earring you own. Here's how to build an everyday stud rotation, style them, and keep them comfortable and bright.
bodyHtml:
Stud earrings are the hardest-working pieces in any jewellery box. They sit flush to the lobe, suit every outfit and disappear into your routine — which is exactly why they are the perfect everyday earring.

This short guide covers the studs worth owning, how to style and layer them, and how to keep them comfortable and bright.

The everyday studs worth owning

A small, considered rotation covers almost any situation. Start with a plain gold-tone dot for office wear and everyday polish, add a pearl stud for soft, timeless elegance, and a sparkling CZ or crystal stud for evenings. Three pairs, endless looks.

How to style and layer studs

Studs are the easiest earring to wear, but they also reward a little styling. Use a simple stud as the anchor of a stacked ear, pairing it with a huggie or small hoop higher up. Match your stud's finish to your other jewellery — gold with gold, silver with silver — for a put-together look, or mix metals deliberately for a modern feel.

Comfort and sensitive ears

Because studs are worn so often, comfort matters most. Pearl Bloom studs use skin-safe, hypoallergenic metal with smooth posts and secure push-backs, so they suit sensitive ears and stay put all day. The anti-tarnish finish means they keep their shine even with constant wear.

Keeping studs bright

A few small habits go a long way: store studs dry and paired so you do not lose one, put them on after perfume and skincare, and wipe them gently with a soft cloth. Treat sparkly and pearl studs a little more gently than plain metal, keeping them away from prolonged moisture.

faqs.q: Are stud earrings good for everyday wear?
faqs.a: Yes. Studs are lightweight, secure and go with everything, making them the ideal everyday earring. An anti-tarnish finish keeps them looking new despite constant wear.

faqs.q: How many pairs of studs should I own?
faqs.a: A simple three-pair rotation works for most people: a plain gold-tone stud, a pearl stud and a sparkly CZ or crystal stud covers daily, office and evening looks.

faqs.q: Can I layer studs with other earrings?
faqs.a: Yes. A simple stud is the perfect anchor for a stacked ear — pair it with a huggie or small hoop in a second piercing for a curated look.

faqs.q: Are these studs good for sensitive ears?
faqs.a: Pearl Bloom studs use skin-safe, hypoallergenic metal with smooth posts, so they are comfortable for sensitive and newly healed ears during all-day wear.

title: How to Style Hoop Earrings for Your Face Shape
metaTitle: How to Style Hoop Earrings for Your Face | Pearl Bloom
metaDescription: Find the best hoop earrings for your face shape — round, oval, square or heart — with sizing and styling tips for an everyday flattering look. Read on.
excerpt: Round, oval, square or heart — the right hoop size and shape can flatter your face beautifully. Here's a simple guide to choosing and styling hoops.
bodyHtml:
Hoop earrings are the ultimate everyday earring — but the right size and shape can do real favours for your face. A few simple guidelines take the guesswork out, so you can pick a flattering pair every time.

Remember these are guidelines, not rules: confidence beats any chart. Use them as a starting point, then wear what you love.

Match the hoop to your face shape

Here is the quick version, by face shape:

Round faces

Larger or slightly angular hoops, and oval or elongated shapes, add length and balance roundness. Avoid very small hoops that can echo the face's curve. Medium-to-large hoops are your friend.

Oval faces

Oval faces suit almost any hoop, from petite to oversized. Feel free to experiment with thickness and texture, including ridged bali styles.

Square faces

Rounded, thinner hoops soften a strong jaw. Go for smooth curves rather than chunky, geometric loops. Huggies and mid-size rounded hoops work well.

Heart-shaped faces

Hoops that are slightly wider at the bottom add balance below a narrower chin. Teardrop-leaning hoops and medium sizes are flattering.

Sizing for the occasion

Size also signals mood. Slim, small hoops and huggies are perfect for daily wear and the office; mid-size hoops are the everyday all-rounder; and large, high-shine hoops bring drama to party wear.

Finish and styling tips

Warm gold-plated hoops flatter most skin tones and suit both Indian and Western looks, while silver-tone reads cooler and more minimal. For a layered ear, stack a small hoop with a simple stud in a second piercing, and keep your necklace simple when wearing larger hoops.

Whatever size you choose, look for lightweight builds and secure closures so the hoops stay comfortable all day.

faqs.q: What size hoops are best for a round face?
faqs.a: Larger or slightly angular hoops, and oval or elongated shapes, are most flattering for round faces because they add length and balance. Very small hoops are less ideal.

faqs.q: Are big hoops suitable for everyday wear?
faqs.a: Mid-size hoops are the best everyday all-rounder. Very large hoops are better for parties, while small hoops and huggies suit daily and office wear.

faqs.q: How do I stop large hoops from feeling heavy?
faqs.a: Choose lightweight designs with balanced weight, as Pearl Bloom hoops are built. This keeps even larger loops comfortable without dragging on the lobe.

faqs.q: Can I layer hoops with other earrings?
faqs.a: Yes. Stacking a small hoop or huggie with a simple stud in a second piercing creates a modern, curated ear. Keep the rest of your jewellery minimal.

title: How to Style Jhumkas & Chandbalis with Indian & Western Outfits
metaTitle: How to Style Jhumkas & Chandbalis | Pearl Bloom
metaDescription: How to style jhumkas and chandbalis with both Indian and Western outfits — face shapes, hairstyles and occasion tips to wear them with confidence.
excerpt: Jhumkas and chandbalis aren't just for saris. Here's how to style India's favourite earrings with ethnic and Western outfits, by face shape and occasion.
bodyHtml:
Jhumkas and chandbalis are the heart of Indian earring style — but they are far more flexible than their festive reputation suggests. Worn well, they elevate everything from a sari to a plain white shirt.

This guide covers how to style jhumkas and chandbalis for different outfits, face shapes and occasions, with affordable, lightweight pairs you can actually wear all day.

Know the two shapes

A jhumka is the bell-domed earring with delicate fringe that chimes as you move — playful, traditional and endlessly wearable. A chandbali is the layered, crescent-moon design — grander and more regal, and a classic for brides. Both come in bright gold-tone, antique oxidised and rich kundan versions.

Styling with Indian outfits

With saris and lehengas, let the earrings anchor the look: a pair of statement chandbalis with minimal or no necklace feels modern and uncluttered. With a simple cotton kurti, a small-to-mid gold-tone jhumka adds just enough character for daily wear. Oxidised jhumkas are perfect with handloom, block-print and indie ethnic pieces.

For festival season and weddings, scale up: ornate jhumkas and chandbalis suit festive wear and wedding wear beautifully, while bridal looks can carry the largest, most detailed designs.

Styling with Western outfits

This is where people are often surprised. A pair of gold-tone jhumkas instantly lifts a plain white shirt, a little black dress or a denim-and-tee combo, adding an unexpected, eclectic touch. Smaller jhumkas work for the office; bolder ones are great for evenings out. Oxidised pairs lean boho and pair well with maxi dresses and earthy tones.

The rule of thumb: the busier the outfit, the simpler the earring — and vice versa.

Face shape and hairstyle tips

Rounder faces are flattered by longer chandbalis and elongated jhumkas that add vertical length, while longer faces suit rounder, fuller jhumkas. To let either shape shine, wear your hair up or swept to one side; loose hair can hide the detailing. If the earrings are large, keep makeup and neckwear minimal so they remain the focal point.

Comfort and care

Traditional jhumkas and chandbalis can be heavy, but Pearl Bloom builds them in lightweight, skin-safe metal so they stay comfortable through long functions. Keep them anti-tarnish bright by storing them dry, putting them on after makeup and perfume, and wiping gently after wear.

faqs.q: Can I wear jhumkas with Western outfits?
faqs.a: Absolutely. Gold-tone jhumkas look striking with a white shirt, a little black dress or jeans and a tee, adding an eclectic touch. Keep them smaller for work and bolder for evenings.

faqs.q: What is the difference between a jhumka and a chandbali?
faqs.a: A jhumka is a bell-domed earring with fringe, while a chandbali is a layered, crescent-moon design. Chandbalis are generally grander and more bridal; jhumkas are more everyday-versatile.

faqs.q: Which jhumka size suits my face shape?
faqs.a: Rounder faces suit longer, elongated jhumkas and chandbalis; longer faces suit rounder, fuller jhumkas. Wearing your hair up helps either shape stand out.

faqs.q: Are jhumkas and chandbalis comfortable for long events?
faqs.a: Pearl Bloom jhumkas and chandbalis are made in lightweight metal, so they keep the traditional look while staying comfortable through long festive and wedding functions.

faqs.q: Should I wear a necklace with statement jhumkas or chandbalis?
faqs.a: Keep it minimal. With large, ornate earrings it is best to skip or simplify the necklace so the earrings remain the focal point of your look.

title: Oxidised vs Gold-Tone vs Silver-Tone: Picking Your Finish
metaTitle: Oxidised vs Gold-Tone vs Silver-Tone Earrings | Pearl Bloom
metaDescription: Oxidised, gold-tone or silver-tone? Compare the three most popular earring finishes on look, care and styling to pick the right one for you. Read more.
excerpt: The same earring looks completely different in gold, silver or oxidised metal. Here's how the three most popular finishes compare on look, styling and care.
bodyHtml:
Shape gets all the attention, but finish is what truly sets the mood of an earring. The exact same hoop can read warm and traditional in gold, crisp and modern in silver, or antique and artisanal when oxidised.

If you are torn between the three most popular Pearl Bloom finishes, here is a clear, side-by-side comparison to help you choose.

Gold-tone: warm, classic, festive

Gold-tone and gold-plated earrings give the warm, rich glow most people picture when they think of jewellery. Gold flatters warm and deep skin tones especially well and is the default choice for festive and traditional looks. It pairs naturally with reds, greens, maroons and earthy tones.

Choose gold-tone if you want a timeless, celebratory feel and a finish that works across both Indian and Western wardrobes.

Silver-tone: cool, clean, contemporary

Silver-tone earrings are bright and cool, with a modern, minimal edge. Silver is a true neutral that pairs effortlessly with greys, blues, blacks, whites and cool pastels, and it coordinates with silver-toned watches and accessories.

Choose silver-tone if you lean minimal and contemporary, or if cool colours dominate your wardrobe.

Oxidised: antique, boho, full of character

Oxidised earrings are deliberately darkened to an antique, silver-grey finish with shadow and depth. The look is rooted in Indian craft and loved for boho, indie and fusion styles. It makes coloured stones and bead work pop, and suits expressive ethnic shapes like jhumkas and bali hoops.

Choose oxidised if you want character and heritage rather than high shine, and love a more artisanal, lived-in look.

How they compare on care

All three are fashion finishes, and all Pearl Bloom pieces are sealed to be anti-tarnish. Gold-tone and silver-tone keep their shine best when stored dry and kept off perfume and lotion. Oxidised metal is intentionally dark, so it hides daily wear well — just avoid harsh polishing, which can strip the antique finish. For the full routine, see our care guide.

So which should you pick?

If you want one versatile starter pair, gold-tone is the safest all-rounder for Indian wardrobes. Add silver-tone for cool, modern outfits and work looks, and bring in oxidised when you want ethnic or boho character. Many people end up owning all three — and because they are affordable, you can.

faqs.q: What is the difference between oxidised, gold-tone and silver-tone earrings?
faqs.a: Gold-tone is warm and classic, silver-tone is cool and modern, and oxidised is a deliberately darkened, antique finish with heritage character. They are all fashion finishes, not solid precious metal.

faqs.q: Which earring finish suits my skin tone?
faqs.a: Gold-tone tends to flatter warm and deep skin tones, while silver-tone suits cool tones especially well. That said, all three can be worn by anyone — personal preference matters most.

faqs.q: Do oxidised earrings tarnish?
faqs.a: The dark look is intentional, not tarnish. Pearl Bloom oxidised earrings are sealed to keep that finish, so they will not dull or go patchy like untreated metal. Avoid harsh polishing to preserve the look.

faqs.q: Which finish is best for festive and wedding wear?
faqs.a: Gold-tone is the traditional choice for festive and wedding looks, while oxidised suits boho and fusion ethnic styles. Silver-tone works well for modern, cool-coloured occasion outfits.

faqs.q: Are all three finishes anti-tarnish?
faqs.a: Yes. Pearl Bloom gold-tone, silver-tone and oxidised earrings are all sealed with an anti-tarnish finish and made from skin-safe, hypoallergenic metal.

title: Earrings for Every Occasion: Daily to Bridal
metaTitle: Earrings for Every Occasion: Daily to Bridal | Pearl Bloom
metaDescription: From daily wear to bridal, find the right earrings for every occasion — office, college, party, festive and wedding looks made easy. Get the guide.
excerpt: What to wear from a regular Tuesday to your best friend's wedding — a simple occasion-by-occasion guide to choosing earrings that fit the moment.
bodyHtml:
The trick to looking put-together is not owning the most jewellery — it is wearing the right earrings for the moment. A pair that is perfect for the office can feel too quiet at a party, and festive jhumkas can overwhelm a regular workday.

Here is a simple, occasion-by-occasion guide to choosing earrings, all drawn from the affordable Pearl Bloom collection so you can shop each look as you go.

Daily wear: light, secure, forgettable (in a good way)

For everyday, you want earrings you can put on and forget. Reach for lightweight studs, slim hoops and huggies in an anti-tarnish finish. Browse the full daily wear edit for pairs that survive real life.

Office wear: polished but understated

Work calls for refinement that does not distract. Small studs, neat huggies and pearl designs are ideal, especially in classic gold-tone. See the office wear collection for desk-to-dinner pieces.

College wear: trend-led and budget-friendly

Campus style is about expressing yourself without overspending. Mix oxidised pieces, fun enamel colour and mismatched pairs. The college wear edit moves easily from lectures to evening plans.

Party wear: bring the sparkle

Evenings are your chance to go bigger. Pick statement earrings, glamorous drops and crystal or American Diamond sparkle. The party wear collection is built to catch the light.

Festive and wedding wear: heritage and grandeur

For festivals and weddings, traditional shapes shine. Jhumkas and chandbalis, often in kundan detailing, are timeless against ethnic outfits. Explore the festive wear and wedding wear edits — and for styling tips, read how to style jhumkas and chandbalis.

Bridal and gifting

Brides and close family can go all-out with the bridal edit — heirloom-style grandeur built to stay light and photograph well. Shopping for someone else? Pre-boxed earring gifts and coordinated earring sets make thoughtful, affordable presents.

faqs.q: What earrings should I wear every day?
faqs.a: Lightweight studs, slim hoops and huggies in an anti-tarnish finish are best for daily wear — comfortable, secure and easy to match with any outfit.

faqs.q: What are the best earrings for the office?
faqs.a: Minimalist studs, small huggies and pearl designs in gold-tone are ideal. They look polished and professional without drawing too much attention.

faqs.q: What earrings go with Indian festive and wedding outfits?
faqs.a: Traditional jhumkas and chandbalis, often with kundan or American Diamond detailing, pair beautifully with saris and lehengas for festive and wedding looks.

faqs.q: Can one pair of earrings work for more than one occasion?
faqs.a: Yes. Many minimal styles cross from daily to office wear, and party pairs often double for festivals. Versatile pieces give you the best value.

faqs.q: What is a good earring gift?
faqs.a: A classic pair of gold-tone or pearl studs, or a pre-boxed earring set, is a safe, elegant and affordable gift suitable for almost anyone.

title: Anti-Tarnish & Waterproof Earrings: How They Work & Care Tips
metaTitle: Anti-Tarnish & Waterproof Earrings Care | Pearl Bloom
metaDescription: How anti-tarnish and waterproof earrings work, plus simple care tips to keep your gold-tone pairs bright and skin-safe for longer. Make them last.
excerpt: What 'anti-tarnish' and 'waterproof' actually mean, why fashion earrings dull, and a simple care routine to keep your gold-tone pairs bright for far longer.
bodyHtml:
If you have ever loved a pair of earrings only to watch them turn dull and dark after a few weeks, you have met tarnish. The good news: anti-tarnish and waterproof earrings are designed to fight exactly that — and a few simple habits make them last even longer.

This guide explains what these terms really mean, then gives you a no-fuss care routine for your Pearl Bloom earrings.

Why fashion earrings tarnish in the first place

Tarnish is a chemical reaction. When the metal in fashion jewellery is exposed to air, moisture, sweat, perfume and skincare, it slowly oxidises — and that reaction shows up as a dull, darkened, sometimes patchy surface. Cheaper, untreated pieces tarnish fastest because the bare metal is fully exposed.

The two biggest accelerators are moisture and chemicals. That is why earrings worn in the shower, at the gym, or sprayed with perfume tend to fade quickest.

How anti-tarnish coatings work

An anti-tarnish earring has a protective coating sealed over the metal. That barrier slows down the contact between the metal and the air, moisture and skin that cause oxidation — so the gold-tone or silver-tone colour stays bright far longer than untreated jewellery.

It is worth being realistic: no coating is permanent. Anti-tarnish dramatically delays dulling, but the finish still benefits from care. The payoff is that a quality gold-plated or gold-tone pair can stay looking new for a long time with very little effort.

What 'waterproof' actually means

Waterproof earrings take protection a step further: they are built and sealed to handle sweat, rain and splashes without fading, which makes them ideal for the gym, the beach and the monsoon. Anti-tarnish resists dulling; waterproof resists water specifically. Many pairs are both.

Even with waterproof designs, we suggest removing heavily embellished or stone-set pairs before long swims or hot showers — not because a quick splash will ruin them, but because prolonged soaking and adhesives behind stones are best kept dry to maximise lifespan.

Your simple earring care routine

Keep this short checklist in mind and your earrings will reward you:

Do

Store them dry in a pouch or box, ideally separated so they do not scratch each other. Put earrings on last — after perfume, hairspray and skincare have settled. Wipe them gently with a soft, dry cloth after wear to remove sweat and oils.

Avoid

Avoid spraying perfume directly onto jewellery, leaving earrings damp, and using harsh chemical cleaners or abrasive cloths, which can strip coatings. Take earrings off before swimming pools (chlorine) and long, hot showers.

Which finishes hold up best

For everyday durability, anti-tarnish gold-plated and gold-tone pieces are the workhorses. Pearl and stone-set designs are a little more delicate and prefer to stay dry, so they last longest with gentle handling. When in doubt, treat sparkle and pearls kindly and let plain metal take the daily knocks.

faqs.q: Do anti-tarnish earrings really work?
faqs.a: Yes. The protective coating slows the oxidation that causes tarnish, so anti-tarnish earrings stay bright much longer than untreated fashion jewellery, especially with simple care like keeping them dry.

faqs.q: Can I shower or swim with waterproof earrings?
faqs.a: Waterproof earrings handle sweat, rain and splashes well. For long, hot showers or swimming pools, it is still best to remove embellished or stone-set pairs to maximise their lifespan.

faqs.q: How long do anti-tarnish earrings last?
faqs.a: With gentle care — stored dry and kept off perfume, lotion and prolonged moisture — a quality anti-tarnish pair holds its colour for a long time. They are also affordable to refresh when needed.

faqs.q: What is the best way to store fashion earrings?
faqs.a: Store them dry in a pouch or box, separated so they do not scratch, and away from humidity. Putting them on after perfume and skincare also protects the finish.

faqs.q: Are anti-tarnish earrings good for sensitive ears?
faqs.a: Yes. They use skin-safe, hypoallergenic metal, and the coating reduces direct contact between your skin and the base metal, which helps comfort for sensitive ears.

title: Types of Earrings: A Complete Guide
metaTitle: Types of Earrings: A Complete Guide | Pearl Bloom
metaDescription: A complete guide to types of earrings — studs, hoops, drops, jhumkas, chandbalis and more, with styling tips to help you pick the right pair. Read on.
excerpt: Studs, hoops, drops, jhumkas, chandbalis and more — a plain-English guide to every type of earring, plus how to choose by finish, face shape and occasion.
bodyHtml:
Earrings are the fastest way to change a look — but with so many shapes, finishes and names, shopping for them can feel confusing. This guide walks through the main types of earrings in plain language, so you can tell a jhumka from a chandbali, a drop from a dangle, and choose the right pair with confidence.

Everything below is part of the affordable, lightweight and anti-tarnish Pearl Bloom earrings collection, so you can read about a style and then shop it in a click.

Three ways to think about earrings

Before the individual shapes, it helps to know that earrings can be sorted three ways — and Pearl Bloom lets you browse by all three:

By style (the shape — studs, hoops, drops and so on), by finish (the colour and material — gold-tone, silver-tone, oxidised, pearl), and by occasion (when you will wear them — daily, office, party, festive, wedding). Most shoppers start with a style or an occasion, then narrow by finish.

The main earring styles, explained

Here are the shapes you will meet most often, from the most minimal to the most dramatic.

Studs

Stud earrings sit flush against the lobe with a small front and a post-and-back fitting. They are the most versatile, comfortable everyday earring and the natural first layer for a stacked ear.

Hoops and huggies

Hoop earrings are rings that pass through the lobe, from thin everyday loops to bold statement circles. Huggies are tiny hoops that hug the lobe closely — great for stacking — while ridged, textured bali hoops add a traditional touch.

Drops and dangles

Drop earrings have a single element that hangs just below the lobe and stays fairly still, while dangle earrings have parts that move and swing. For real length, long earrings fall well past the lobe to lengthen the neck.

Jhumkas and chandbalis

These are India's much-loved traditional shapes. The jhumka is a bell-domed earring with delicate fringe, while the chandbali is a layered, crescent-moon design favoured for weddings and festivals.

Statement, ear cuffs and more

Statement earrings are bold and architectural — the one accessory that finishes a look. Ear cuffs and clip-ons need no piercing, and mismatch pairs are two coordinated-but-different earrings worn together.

Finishes that change the whole look

The same shape feels completely different depending on its finish. Warm gold-plated and gold-tone read classic and festive; cool silver-tone reads clean and modern; and darkened oxidised metal brings antique, boho character.

Then there are the materials that add colour and sparkle: soft pearl, brilliant CZ and American Diamond, glossy enamel and traditional kundan. Not sure which to pick? Our finishes comparison guide breaks down the three most popular metal tones.

Matching earrings to the occasion

Finally, think about where you will wear them. Light daily wear and minimalist office wear call for small studs and slim hoops; party wear welcomes sparkle and scale; and festive, wedding and bridal looks suit ornate jhumkas and chandbalis. For a deeper dive, read earrings for every occasion.

Keeping fashion earrings looking new

Because these are fashion earrings rather than solid gold, the right care keeps them bright for far longer. Choose anti-tarnish designs, store them dry, put them on after perfume and skincare, and wipe them gently now and then. Our anti-tarnish and waterproof care guide explains exactly how the coatings work.

faqs.q: What are the most common types of earrings?
faqs.a: The most common types are studs, hoops, drops and dangles, plus traditional Indian styles like jhumkas and chandbalis. Studs and hoops are the most versatile for everyday wear.

faqs.q: Which earrings are best for everyday wear?
faqs.a: Lightweight studs, slim hoops and huggies are best for everyday wear because they are comfortable, secure and go with everything. Anti-tarnish finishes keep them looking new.

faqs.q: Are fashion earrings safe for sensitive ears?
faqs.a: Yes, when they use skin-safe, hypoallergenic metal with smooth posts, as Pearl Bloom earrings do. Anti-tarnish coatings also reduce skin contact with the base metal.

faqs.q: What is the difference between gold-plated and gold-tone earrings?
faqs.a: Gold-plated earrings have an actual layer of gold-tone metal bonded over a core, while gold-tone refers to any finish that gives a gold colour. Both offer a gold look affordably; neither is solid gold.

faqs.q: How do I stop fashion earrings from tarnishing?
faqs.a: Choose anti-tarnish pairs, keep them dry, store them in a pouch, apply perfume and lotion before wearing them, and wipe them with a soft cloth. These habits keep the shine for much longer.
